source.title: DLM-Scope: Mechanistic Interpretability of Diffusion Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xu Wang; Bin Jiang; Yunyang Wan; Bao-Song Yang; Lingpeng Kong; Di-Fan Zou

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE-feature stability across denoising steps and transfer between base and instruction-tuned models, bearing on whether SAE features are stable representation units. It does not test the original toy-model geometry.
record.gate_note: Rows cover feature-dynamics and transfer results relevant to V5. SAE-steering results are induced interventions, and decoding-order accuracy results do not directly measure any listed version, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains Top-K SAEs on two diffusion language models (Dream-7B, LLaDA-8B), a new setting. It asks whether they recover sparse, interpretable features that reconstruct activations faithfully (Sections 3.2–3.3). That bears on V4: real models contain sparse features a dictionary can recover. The decoding-order dynamics measure how token representations change across denoising steps, not whether SAE features are canonical units. The base-to-SFT transfer measures insertion loss of a reused dictionary, not feature identity or canonicality. So neither tests V5 as stated. Steering results are induced interventions and are excluded.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is incomplete. The authors conclude that Top-K SAEs trained on DLMs give faithful, interpretable features. They report that SAE insertion in early DLM layers can reduce cross-entropy, unlike in LLMs, and that diffusion-time SAE steering often outperforms LLM steering. They also find that SAE feature dynamics give signals that track decoding-order performance, and that base-trained SAEs transfer to the instruction-tuned model except at the deepest layer.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains Top-K sparse autoencoders on diffusion-language-model activations and measures their feature dynamics and transfer; it does not reproduce the toy-network feature-overlap experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature dynamics vary with decoding order and layer depth; base-to-SFT transfer is weaker at L27 than at L1–L23.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE top-k feature sets for masked positions shift early, then settle, under confidence-based decoding. Decoded positions keep drifting in deep layers. ORIGIN changes little. Top-1 identity is largely stable throughout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature trajectories across denoising steps differ by decoding order and correlate with task accuracy in diffusion LMs.

fits_no_version.finding: A base-trained SAE gives near-identical insertion ΔLoss to an SFT-trained SAE in Dream SFT at L1–L23. At L27 the curves separate, especially on instruction rollouts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries transfer across instruction tuning except at the deepest layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Inserting SAEs in shallow DLM layers at small L0 can reduce masked-token cross-entropy (negative ΔLoss). The effect is absent or weaker in autoregressive LLMs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction can act as a beneficial denoiser in early layers of diffusion LMs.

record.problems: Feature-stability and transfer findings are described qualitatively in the text; the corresponding figures do not have numerical values transcribed in the provided text. Uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on a tested version were left out.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy networks, geometry, or sparsity transition.
All parts: no capacity or feature-importance analysis of neurons.
Whether features spread across many neurons (no neuron-level polysemanticity analysis). Also LLM-side SAE interpretability: the Qwen/LLaMA SAEs are used only as fidelity and steering baselines.
Completeness, stability across seeds or dictionary sizes, and canonicality of SAE features. None is measured; transfer is assessed by insertion loss without matching features.
All parts: no test of one- versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Sparsity-fidelity sweeps (explained variance and ΔLM loss vs L0, per layer) for Dream, LLaDA, Qwen and LLaMA SAEs
Auto-interpretability scores of DLM-SAE features (example scores 0.85, 0.90, 0.31; appendix examples 1.00, 0.714, 0.929, 0.286). No aggregate is reported.

record.verdict_notes: All results bearing on V4 are figure-only or illustrative examples, with no aggregate interpretability score and no uncertainty. The record's V5 links were dropped: the dynamics and transfer measures concern representation change and reconstruction transfer, not whether SAE features are canonical or complete units. Steering (Table 2) is correctly excluded as an induced intervention. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from capacity pressure or feature importance.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or are recoverable by dictionaries; the study concerns diffusion language models, not that LLM claim.
Whether SAE features are complete or canonical units; the study measures interpretability, stability across denoising, and transfer, not completeness or canonicality.
Whether represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Dream-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured step-to-step pre-mask SAE top-k feature-set Jaccard similarity.
rows.measure: Pre-mask top-k feature-set similarity between consecutive denoising steps
rows.value: Features change only slightly from step to step; ORIGIN yields a less dynamic SAE trajectory.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative description; no plotted values are stated.
rows.check: Jaccard overlap of top-k features between consecutive denoising steps measures how a token's representation evolves during generation. It does not show SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units, so it is not V5. Qualitative only, with no baseline.

rows.subject: Dream-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured step-to-step pre-mask SAE top-k feature-set Jaccard similarity.
rows.measure: Pre-mask top-k feature-set similarity between consecutive denoising steps
rows.value: Features shift more early for still-masked tokens, then settle quickly.
rows.note: Qualitative result; values are not stated.
rows.check: Same construct as R1: representation dynamics across decoding orders, not dictionary canonicality. 'Partial' has no meaning against V5 here.

rows.subject: Dream-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured post-decode SAE feature drift for positions after their tokens were fixed.
rows.note: Qualitative result; values are not stated.
rows.check: Post-decode drift tracks representation change after a token is fixed. This is a property of the DLM, not of SAE features as units.

rows.subject: Dream-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured post-decode SAE feature drift for positions after their tokens were fixed.
rows.value: Confidence-based orders sustain stronger deep-layer drift; deep-layer features continue adjusting after tokens are fixed.
rows.note: Qualitative result; values are not stated.
rows.check: Same as R3. Deep-layer drift under confidence-based orders is the model's behaviour and does not bear on V5.

rows.subject: Dream-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured whether the top-1 SAE feature identity stays unchanged between consecutive steps at masked positions.
rows.value: Top-1 feature identity is described as largely stable, with a high lock rate.
rows.note: The text states the qualitative result; no numeric lock-rate values are given.
rows.check: Top-1 lock rate across denoising steps concerns temporal consistency of a token's dominant feature, not stability of the dictionary across seeds or sizes. Qualitative only (Appendix H).

rows.subject: Dream-7B
rows.operation_detail: Counted changes in top-1 SAE feature identity between consecutive steps at decoded positions.
rows.value: Top-1 feature identity is described as largely stable, with few flips.
rows.note: The text states the qualitative result; no numeric flip counts are given.

rows.value: Base-trained and SFT-trained SAEs show nearly identical functional behavior at these layers.

relationships.condition: Dream-7B and LLaDA-8B residual-stream Top-K SAEs, shallow and middle layers
relationships.reason: Based on the text, since no row records it: SAEs reach a favorable sparsity-fidelity profile, with EV rising with L0 (Fig. 3, Fig. 8). Auto-interpretation yields interpretable features (e.g. 0.85 and 0.90 scores). Values are figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: The SAEs reached a favorable sparsity-fidelity profile, with explained variance rising with L0, and auto-interpretation found interpretable features, with scores such as 0.85 and 0.90.

relationships.condition: Deep layers and some individual features
relationships.reason: Based on the text: deeper layers need larger L0 to reach comparable EV, and overly sparse SAEs there cause larger loss deviations (App. C). Some features score low (0.31, 0.286).
relationships.display_finding: Deeper layers needed a larger L0 to reach comparable explained variance, and overly sparse SAEs there caused larger loss deviations. Some features scored low (0.31, 0.286).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Top-1 feature identity across all three tested decoding orders; Dream SFT layers L1–L23
reader_labels.reason: Top-1 identities are described as largely stable with few flips, and base-trained SAEs transfer similarly to SFT-trained SAEs at L1–L23 (R5, R6, R7, R9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Top-k feature dynamics under confidence-based decoding orders and Dream SFT layer L27
reader_labels.reason: Confidence-based orders show early feature shifts and continued deep-layer drift; transfer also breaks down at L27, where the base-trained SAE causes a much larger rollout loss increase (R2, R4, R8, R10).
